title: Cellular Senescence. SkinMed investing in Senotherapeutics (Senomorphics and Senolytics) Research - SkinMed
abstract:
While the exact mechanisms are still being fully elucidated, it is thought to influence pathways related to cellular longevity and resilience, potentially by improving protein homeostasis or reducing oxidative stress, thereby delaying the onset of senescence in skin cells like fibroblasts and melanocytes  
Senotherapeutics are a class of compounds that target senescent cells, either by eliminating them (senolytics) or by modulating their harmful effects, particularly the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP) (senomorphics).  
While many senotherapeutics do possess antioxidant properties, their primary mechanism of action goes beyond simply neutralizing free radicals, directly addressing the root cause of cellular senescence.  
There a number of prospective topical and oral agents classified as senotherapeutics/senolytics that offer more than just antioxidant benefits, with a focus on their impact on skin:  
**Topical Agents (Senolytics & Senomorphics for Skin):**  
- Topical compounds which targets anti-apoptotic cells and thereby induces senescent cell programmed death, also decreases inflammation, accelerates wound healing and tsargets dysfunctional cells
- There are senomorphics which suppress the SASP (Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype) without necessarily killing senescent cells  
<!--THE END-->  
- **Another compound exhibits both**  
<!--THE END-->  
- **A Senolytic effect:**It’s claimed to induce apoptosis in senescent cells.
<!--THE END-->  
- **A Senolytic effect:**It’s claimed to induce apoptosis in senescent cells.
- **A Senomorphic effect:**It inhibits the secretion of SASP factors like interleukins (IL-6, IL-8) and collagenase (MMP-1), preventing the spread of senescence and restoring fibroblast function (this may be dangerous if senescence is a last resort pathway to prevent the cell becoming malignant).  
<!--THE END-->  
- Some peptides are being investigated for their senotherapeutic properties, acting as senomorphics by reducing biological age markers in skin and improving skin health, potentially outperforming traditional anti-aging ingredients like retinol.
- Their mechanism often involves influencing cellular signalling pathways to promote youthful cell behaviour, rather than solely antioxidation.  
<!--THE END-->  
- **Natural Extracts/Botanicals with Senolytic/Senomorphic Properties (e.g., EGCG, Curcumin, Fisetin, Quercetin both topical but maybe better as a supplement**  
While these compounds are well-known antioxidants, their classification as senolytics or senomorphics highlights their ability to selectively eliminate senescent cells or modulate the SASP.  
- **Epigallocatechin Gallate (EGCG) from green tea:**Shown to lower the number of senescent fibroblasts in skin and suppress SASP factors.  
<!--THE END-->  
- **Curcumin from turmeric:**Exhibits senolytic activity and can enhance the efficacy of other senolytics.  
<!--THE END-->
<!--THE END-->  
- **Fisetin (from apples, strawberries):**Considered a potent senolytic, capable of reducing SASP factors and reversing senescence in fibroblasts.  
<!--THE END-->  
- **Quercetin (from various fruits and vegetables):**While an antioxidant, it also acts as a senolytic, particularly in combination with other compounds, by targeting anti-apoptotic pathways in senescent cells.  
**Oral Agents (Senolytics & Senomorphics):**  
- **A cancer drug combined with Quercetin**(a flavonoid) work synergistically to selectively induce apoptosis in senescent cells by targeting anti-apoptotic pathways.  
This combination has been shown to improve age-related conditions in animal models and is undergoing human clinical trials for various age-related diseases, including those with skin manifestations.  
- **Fisetin:**As mentioned above, fisetin is a potent senolytic and can be taken orally. It’s more effective at reducing SASP factors and reversing senescence than some other natural compounds, and has shown promise in animal studies for anti-aging effects.  
**Metformin:** Primarily an anti-diabetic drug, metformin is also considered a senomorphic due to its ability to inhibit pathways implicated in cellular senescence and SASP production. It has shown promise in extending lifespan in animal studies and is being investigated in human trials (TAME trial) for its anti-aging effects, including potential benefits for skin aging.
